**TEDS asks whether the predicted table has the right tree structure and, depending on the variant, the right cell contents.** HTML represents a table as nested elements: table, rows, and cells. Tree edit distance measures the cost of transforming one such structure into another. Normalizing that cost gives a similarity score. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.10683)

A predicted cell can overlap the correct image region almost perfectly while claiming the wrong row span. Bounding-box IoU would look good, but the table's structure would be wrong. Conversely, two structurally identical tables can differ in one digit that changes a reported value by a factor of ten.

**A numerical illustration.** Under a chosen edit-cost implementation, suppose the larger tree has 20 nodes and the edit distance is 3. The normalized similarity is $1-3/20=0.85$. The actual edit rules matter: replacing cell text may be scored differently from adding or deleting a structural node.

Use structure-only TEDS to isolate layout errors and a content-aware version to include text. Add exact or task-specific numerical accuracy when small character errors have large consequences. Canonicalize equivalent markup consistently, since different HTML strings can describe the same table. No single score captures geometry, structure, and semantic correctness completely; choose complementary metrics that reveal which aspect failed.

**Technical details and references.**

TEDS compares predicted and reference table trees using normalized edit cost, reflecting structural changes such as missing cells or wrong spans and, in content-aware variants, cell text differences. A common form is [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.10683)

$$TEDS=1-\frac{EditDist(T_p,T_r)}{\max(|T_p|,|T_r|)}.$$

Bounding-box IoU measures spatial overlap but may assign a good score to a cell attached to the wrong row/header or with an incorrect span. Conversely, tree similarity alone may hide small numeric transcription errors with large business impact. Report structure-only and content-aware variants, text/numeric accuracy, and geometric metrics together. Canonicalize equivalent HTML consistently and specify the edit-cost implementation; raw HTML-string similarity is not the same as DOM-tree correctness.
